title: The Number of Latin Tableaux of Shape $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ is $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$ for Every $k \ge 5$
abstract: Latin tableaux generalize Latin squares to Young diagrams. In arXiv:2610.29291, Conjecture 6.3 asks whether for every integer $k \ge 5$, the number of Latin tableaux of shape $\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ and type $\lambda'$ is given by the closed formula $LT(\lambda) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$. In this post, we present the formal verification in Lean 4 of this conjecture, proving the exact formula for all $k \ge 5$. The proof shows that the column contents of every Latin tableau of shape $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ follow one rigid pattern, and deduces that every such tableau admits exactly four valid extensions when a new top row of length $k+1$ is adjoined. Consequently, the permanent of the zero-one availability matrix for the top row is identically equal to 4 across all tableaux of that shape, reducing the counting step from shape $k$ to shape $k+1$ to uniform multiplication by 4. Combined with an exact evaluation of the base case $k = 5$, where there are exactly 144 Latin tableaux of shape $(5, 4, 3, 3)$ matching $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$, the general formula follows by induction. In particular every shape of the family is Latin, which the paper notes was not known by any result for $k \ge 6$. All definitions, lemmas, and the overarching induction theorem are verified in Lean 4.
introduction:
A Latin tableau is a filling of a Young diagram whose entries satisfy Latin properties along its rows and columns. Specifically, for a partition $\mu$, a Latin tableau of shape $\mu$ and type $\mu'$ is a filling of the cells of $\mu$ with positive integers such that the entries in each row $i$ are chosen from $\{1, \dots, \mu_i\}$ without repetition, and no positive integer appears more than once in any column. Since row $i$ contains exactly $\mu_i$ cells, the distinctness condition implies that each row $i$ is filled with a permutation of the set $\{1, 2, \dots, \mu_i\}$. When the Young diagram is a square of size $n \times n$, these structures correspond to standard Latin squares of order $n$. For non-rectangular diagrams, the interaction between row-length bounds and column distinctness constraints introduces intricate combinatorial dependencies.

The study of Latin tableaux and their exact enumeration for infinite families of shapes was investigated in arXiv:2610.29291. Among the partition families considered in that work are staircase diagrams and staircase-like shapes with modified tails. A specific family of shapes consists of those with a double-three staircase tail: for an integer $k \ge 5$, the partition $\lambda$ is defined by the sequence of row lengths
$$\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3).$$
This diagram has $k-1$ nonempty rows: the first row has length $k$, each subsequent row decreases in length by 1 until length 3 is reached, and the final two rows both have length 3.

In arXiv:2610.29291, Conjecture 6.3 posed the question of whether the number of Latin tableaux of shape $\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ and type $\lambda'$, denoted by $LT(\lambda)$, is given by the exact exponential formula
$$LT(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$$
for every integer $k \ge 5$. For the smallest parameter value $k = 5$, the partition is $(5, 4, 3, 3)$, and the conjectured formula predicts $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$ Latin tableaux. The paper reports 576 tableaux for $k = 6$, in agreement with the formula, observes that every filling of $(6,5,4,3,3)$ has $4$, $5$, $6$ in the first three cells of the top row and $1$, $2$, $3$ in the last three, and notes that no shape of the family with $k \ge 6$ was known to be Latin by any result.

The difficulty in establishing such an enumeration directly lies in the recursive nature of Young diagram extensions. Adding a new top row of length $k+1$ above a tableau of shape $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ requires placing a permutation of $\{1, 2, \dots, k+1\}$ such that no entry conflicts with any entry already present in the same column. In general, the number of ways to complete such a row depends on the specific entries appearing in the columns of the underlying tableau $T$. The count of completions for a given tableau $T$ can be expressed as the permanent of a $(k+1) \times (k+1)$ zero-one matrix, known as the top-row availability matrix. Because matrix permanents can vary across different tableaux of the same shape, sums of permanents over large sets of tableaux typically resist closed-form simplification unless strong structural uniformity is present.

In this post, we report on the complete formal resolution of Conjecture 6.3 in Lean 4 via the theorem `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula`. The proof first establishes a rigid column pattern shared by all tableaux of the family, and from it a structural regularity: for every integer $k \ge 5$, every Latin tableau of shape $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ admits exactly four valid extensions to a Latin tableau of shape $(k+1, k, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$. That is, the permanent of the availability matrix is not merely 4 on average; it is pointwise invariant, equal to 4 for every single tableau in the family. This pointwise extension property turns the summation over all tableaux into a scalar multiplication by 4, reducing the inductive step to an elementary recurrence. With the base case $k = 5$ formally established, the closed formula $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$ holds for all $k \ge 5$.
result:
The main theorem establishes the validity of Conjecture 6.3 from arXiv:2610.29291, giving an exact exponential formula for the number of Latin tableaux with a double-three staircase tail.

Theorem (`latin_double_three_tail_count_formula`). For every integer $k \ge 5$, the number of Latin tableaux of shape $\lambda(k) = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ and type $\lambda(k)'$ is given by
$$LT(\lambda(k)) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}.$$

In Lean 4, the theorem is named `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula`. The statement takes a natural number $k$, assumes the hypothesis $5 \le k$, applies `latin_double_three_tail_shape` to construct the Young diagram, and asserts that `latin_tableaux_count` equals $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$.

In addition to the main formula, the formal development provides three foundational results:

- Base-case enumeration (`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`): For $k = 5$, the Young diagram has shape $(5, 4, 3, 3)$, and the number of Latin tableaux is exactly 144, verifying $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$.
- Inductive step formula (`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`): For every $k \ge 5$, the number of Latin tableaux of shape $\lambda(k+1)$ equals the sum of the permanents of the top-row availability matrices over all Latin tableaux of shape $\lambda(k)$.
- Pointwise four-extension property (`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`): For every $k \ge 5$ and every Latin tableau $T$ of shape $\lambda(k)$, the permanent of the top-row availability matrix of width $k+1$ is identically equal to 4.
proof:
We present the proof of `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` following the formal argument verified in Lean 4.

The idea of the proof is an induction on $k \ge 5$. The base case at $k = 5$ is verified by exhaustive computation on the finite set of tableaux of shape $(5, 4, 3, 3)$. For the inductive step, adjoining a row of length $k+1$ at the top of a tableau of shape $\lambda(k) = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ yields a tableau of shape $\lambda(k+1) = (k+1, k, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$. The number of ways to fill this top row without violating column distinctness equals the permanent of the availability matrix. Every tableau of shape $\lambda(k)$ has the same rigid pattern of column contents, and from it its availability permanent is identically equal to 4, so the sum of permanents factors into 4 times the cardinality of `latin_tableaux` of shape $\lambda(k)$. Applying the induction hypothesis reduces the step to elementary exponent arithmetic.

Lemma 1 (`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`). The number of Latin tableaux of shape $(5, 4, 3, 3)$ satisfies
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } 5) = 144.$$

*Proof of Lemma 1.* The Young diagram $\lambda(5)$ has row lengths $(5, 4, 3, 3)$, which contain $5 + 4 + 3 + 3 = 15$ cells in total. A tableau is an assignment of values in $\{1, \dots, \lambda(5).\text{rowLen}(i)\}$ to each cell $(i, j)$ such that entries are distinct along each row and distinct along each column. Because the cell set is finite and the set of possible fillings is finite, Lean evaluates the cardinality of the filtered finset of Latin tableaux. The computation searches through all valid row permutations satisfying column injectivity across the 15 cells. The verification confirms that exactly 144 fillings satisfy all constraints. Noting that $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 4^2 = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$, the base case holds.

Lemma 2 (`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`). For any integer $k \ge 5$, the number of Latin tableaux of shape $\lambda(k+1)$ satisfies
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape}(k+1)) = \sum_{T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)} \text{Matrix.permanent}(\text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)).$$

*Proof of Lemma 2.* This is the case of inserting a new first row in the paper's own permanent recursion (its Lemma 5.4). Any tableau $T'$ of shape $\lambda(k+1) = (k+1, k, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ decomposes uniquely into its top row (row 0 of length $k+1$) and the remaining $k-1$ rows. Shifting the lower rows upward by one index produces a tableau $T$ of shape $\lambda(k) = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$. The entries of row 0 must form a permutation of $\{1, 2, \dots, k+1\}$ such that for every column $j \in \{0, \dots, k\}$, the value placed in $(0, j)$ does not appear in column $j$ of $T$. In terms of the availability matrix $M = \text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)$, entry $M_{i, j}$ equals 1 if and only if symbol $i+1$ is available in column $j$. A valid top row is therefore a bijection $\sigma : \{0, \dots, k\} \to \{0, \dots, k\}$ such that $M_{\sigma(j), j} = 1$ for all $j$. The number of such bijections is the permanent of $M$. Summing over all valid completions of all tableaux $T$ of shape $\lambda(k)$ yields the identity.

Lemma 3 (`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`). For any integer $k \ge 5$ and every Latin tableau $T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)$, the permanent of the top-row availability matrix of width $k+1$ is 4:
$$\text{Matrix.permanent}(\text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)) = 4.$$

*Proof of Lemma 3.* The Lean proof goes through the symbol sets of the columns. In $\lambda(k)$ (columns indexed from 0), columns $0, 1, 2$ have $k-1$ cells each and column $j$ has $k-j$ cells for $3 \le j \le k-1$; in particular column $k-2$ has two cells and column $k-1$ has one. Say a tableau $T$ of shape $\lambda(k)$ has the *canonical profile* if there are $s \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $c \in \{0,1,2\}$ such that

- column $c$ contains the symbols $\{1, \dots, k-2\} \cup \{k\}$, and the other two of the columns $0, 1, 2$ contain $\{1, \dots, k-1\}$;
- column $j$ contains $\{1, \dots, k-j\}$ for $3 \le j \le k-3$;
- column $k-2$ contains $\{1,2,3\} \setminus \{s\}$, and column $k-1$ contains $\{s\}$.

*Step (a): every tableau of shape $\lambda(k)$, $k \ge 5$, has the canonical profile.* This is an induction on $k$. For $k = 5$ it is checked over all tableaux of shape $(5,4,3,3)$. For the step, a tableau of shape $\lambda(k+1)$ is a tableau $T$ of shape $\lambda(k)$ with a top row of length $k+1$ placed above it; by induction $T$ has the canonical profile, and the analysis of step (b) below shows which symbols the top row can place in each column. Adding them to the column sets of $T$ gives the canonical profile of shape $\lambda(k+1)$: the two columns among $0, 1, 2$ holding $\{1,\dots,k-1\}$ receive $k$ and $k+1$, one becoming $\{1,\dots,k\}$ and the other $\{1,\dots,k-1\} \cup \{k+1\}$; column $c$ receives $k-1$ and becomes $\{1,\dots,k\}$; column $j$ with $3 \le j \le k-3$ receives $k-j+1$; column $k-2$ receives $s$ and becomes $\{1,2,3\}$; and columns $k-1$ and $k$ receive the two symbols of $\{1,2,3\} \setminus \{s\}$, so that column $k-1$ holds two of $\{1,2,3\}$ and column $k$ holds the third.

*Step (b): a tableau with the canonical profile has exactly four valid top rows of length $k+1$.* A top row is a bijection from the columns $0, \dots, k$ to the symbols $1, \dots, k+1$ with no symbol placed in a column that already contains it. The two columns among $0, 1, 2$ holding $\{1,\dots,k-1\}$ can only take $k$ and $k+1$, so they take exactly these two symbols, in one of two orders. Column $c$ can then only take $k-1$. Going right, column $j$ for $j = 3, \dots, k-3$ can only take symbols at least $k-j+1$, and all larger ones are used, so it takes $k-j+1$; this uses up $4, \dots, k-2$. The symbols $1, 2, 3$ remain for columns $k-2$, $k-1$, $k$. Column $k-2$ contains $\{1,2,3\} \setminus \{s\}$, so it takes $s$, and columns $k-1$ and $k$ take the other two in either order (column $k-1$ contains only $s$, and column $k$ is empty). That gives $2 \cdot 2 = 4$ top rows, so the permanent of the availability matrix is 4.

*Proof of the Main Theorem.* We combine Lemmas 1, 2, and 3 to prove `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` by induction on $k \ge 5$.

In the base case $k = 5$, Lemma 1 (`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`) establishes that
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } 5) = 144.$$
Since $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 4^2 = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$, the base case holds by direct numerical evaluation.

For the induction step, assume as the induction hypothesis that for some $k \ge 5$,
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}.$$
We wish to compute the count for $k+1$. Applying Lemma 2 (`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`), we write the count of tableaux of shape $\lambda(k+1)$ as
$$\sum_{T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)} \text{Matrix.permanent}(\text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)).$$
By Lemma 3 (`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`), each term in this sum is identically 4. Replacing each permanent by 4 across the summation gives
$$\sum_{T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)} 4.$$
Summing the constant 4 over the finite set of Latin tableaux produces the product
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \cdot 4.$$
Substituting the induction hypothesis into this expression yields
$$(9 \cdot 4^{k-3}) \cdot 4.$$
Because $k \ge 5$, the exponent arithmetic satisfies $(k+1) - 3 = (k - 3) + 1$, and by the law of exponents $4^{(k-3)+1} = 4^{k-3} \cdot 4$. Rewriting the product gives
$$9 \cdot 4^{(k+1)-3},$$
which completes the inductive step and proves the theorem for all $k \ge 5$.
discussion:
The theorem `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` completely settles Conjecture 6.3 of arXiv:2610.29291. The question as posed asked whether the number of Latin tableaux of shape $\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ and type $\lambda'$ is equal to $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$ for every integer $k \ge 5$. The theorem establishes this equality in full generality, answering the question affirmatively for the entire infinite family.

Since $9 \cdot 4^{k-3} > 0$, every shape $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ with $k \ge 5$ is Latin. The paper points out that none of these shapes for $k \ge 6$ was known to be Latin by any result, and that already for $(6,5,4,3,3)$ a new technique would be needed; the column-profile argument above is one, for the whole family.

The proof strategy relies on the pointwise four-extension property formulated in Lemma 3 (`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`), combined with the inductive step in Lemma 2 (`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`) and the base evaluation in Lemma 1 (`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`). In general counting problems for Latin tableaux, the number of ways to extend a tableau by a new row can vary substantially depending on the column entries of the individual tableau. Here, however, every tableau of shape $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ has an availability matrix whose permanent is identically equal to 4. This uniform behavior reduces the sum of permanents in the step formula directly to scalar multiplication by 4.

Regarding what the result does not cover, the enumeration applies strictly to the family of Young diagrams with a double-three staircase tail:

- The theorem is stated for $k \ge 5$, the range of Conjecture 6.3; smaller $k$ are not treated.
- The result does not cover tableaux of shapes other than $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$, such as staircases with different tail lengths or Young diagrams with other partition structures.

Finally, the provided source material names no further open questions or conjectures beyond Conjecture 6.3. Because `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` proves the exact formula for all $k \ge 5$, the question posed in arXiv:2610.29291 regarding this infinite family is completely closed.
preliminaries:
To formalize the enumeration in Lean 4, we define Young diagrams, the family of double-three tail partitions, the set of Latin tableaux, and the top-row availability matrix. We adhere to the mathematical and Lean structures provided in the library.

A Young diagram $\mu$ is represented as a collection of cells $(i, j) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ arranged in rows and columns, where $i$ denotes the row index and $j$ denotes the column index. In the Lean formalization, both row and column indices are 0-indexed, so the top-left cell of the diagram is $(0, 0)$. The length of row $i$ is denoted by $\mu.\text{rowLen}(i)$.

Definition 1 (`latin_double_three_tail_shape`). For an integer $k \ge 5$, the Young diagram with a double-three staircase tail, denoted $\lambda(k)$, is the partition whose $i$-th row length for $0 \le i < k-1$ is given by
$$\lambda(k).\text{rowLen}(i) = \max(3, k - i),$$
and whose rows are empty for all $i \ge k-1$. In sequence notation, the row lengths of $\lambda(k)$ are
$$(k, k-1, k-2, \dots, 4, 3, 3),$$
comprising exactly $k-1$ nonempty rows. For example, when $k = 5$, the diagram $\lambda(5)$ has row lengths $(5, 4, 3, 3)$. For $k = 6$, the row lengths are $(6, 5, 4, 3, 3)$.

Remark on indexing and empty rows. The Lean definition `latin_double_three_tail_shape` specifies row lengths using the 0-indexed formula $\max(3, k - i)$ strictly for $i < k - 1$. For all $i \ge k - 1$, the row length is implicitly 0. Thus, exactly $k - 1$ rows are nonempty. The final two nonempty rows, at indices $i = k - 3$ and $i = k - 2$, both have length $\max(3, 3) = 3$ and $\max(3, 2) = 3$, creating the double-three tail.

Definition 2 (`latin_tableaux`). Let $\mu$ be a Young diagram. A Latin tableau of shape $\mu$ and type $\mu'$ is a filling $T : \mu.\text{cells} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfying the following conditions:

- Row-length bounds: For each cell $c = (i, j) \in \mu.\text{cells}$, the entry $T(c)$ belongs to the discrete interval $\{1, 2, \dots, \mu.\text{rowLen}(i)\}$.
- Row distinctness: For any two cells $c_1 = (i_1, j_1)$ and $c_2 = (i_2, j_2)$ in $\mu.\text{cells}$ with $i_1 = i_2$, if $T(c_1) = T(c_2)$, then $j_1 = j_2$.
- Column distinctness: For any two cells $c_1 = (i_1, j_1)$ and $c_2 = (i_2, j_2)$ in $\mu.\text{cells}$ with $j_1 = j_2$, if $T(c_1) = T(c_2)$, then $i_1 = i_2$.

The set of all such Latin tableaux on $\mu$ is denoted by `latin_tableaux` $\mu$.

Remark on row permutations. Because row $i$ contains exactly $\mu.\text{rowLen}(i)$ cells and each cell takes a value in $\{1, \dots, \mu.\text{rowLen}(i)\}$, the row injectivity condition guarantees that the sequence of entries in row $i$ is a permutation of $\{1, \dots, \mu.\text{rowLen}(i)\}$. In contrast, column lengths vary across the diagram, and the column condition requires that no symbol is repeated within any column.

Definition 3 (`latin_tableaux_count`). For a Young diagram $\mu$, the count of Latin tableaux of shape $\mu$ and type $\mu'$, denoted $LT(\mu)$, is the cardinality of the finset `latin_tableaux` $\mu$:
$$LT(\mu) = \#(\text{latin\_tableaux}(\mu)).$$

Definition 4 (`latin_top_row_availability`). Let $d$ be a Young diagram, let $T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(d)$, and let $w \in \mathbb{N}$ denote the width of a prospective top row to be added above $T$. The top-row availability matrix of $T$ for width $w$ is the $w \times w$ matrix over $\mathbb{N}$, denoted $A(d, T, w)$, defined for indices $i, j \in \{0, 1, \dots, w-1\}$ by
$$A(d, T, w)_{i, j} = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{if for all } c \in d.\text{cells} \text{ with } c.\text{col} = j, \text{ we have } T(c) \neq i + 1, \\
0 & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}$$

Remark on prospective symbols and columns. In `latin_top_row_availability`, the matrix rows index prospective symbols $s = i + 1 \in \{1, \dots, w\}$, while the matrix columns index tableau columns $j \in \{0, \dots, w-1\}$. An entry is 1 precisely when placing symbol $i + 1$ into column $j$ creates no column conflict with any cell in column $j$ of $T$. A valid placement of a complete top row of length $w$ corresponds to a bijection between symbols and columns with availability 1, and the total number of such valid top rows is given by the permanent of $A(d, T, w)$.

problem.title: Exact enumeration of Latin tableaux with a double-three staircase tail

research: settles OP-512 (Exact enumeration of Latin tableaux with a double-three staircase tail)
tier_why: Settles the paper's Conjecture 6.3 for the whole family k >= 5 (exact count, and Latinness of every shape, unknown for k >= 6), by a column-profile induction; a specific conjecture of the paper's final section, not its central question.

zh.title: 对每个 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的拉丁杨表数目为 $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$
zh.abstract: 拉丁杨表（LT）将拉丁方推广到杨图。在 arXiv:2610.29291 中，猜想 6.3 探讨对于每个整数 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 且型为 $\lambda'$ 的拉丁杨表数目是否由闭形式公式 $LT(\lambda) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$ 给出。在本篇博文中，我们介绍了该猜想在 Lean 4 中的形式化验证，证明了对所有 $k \ge 5$ 该精确公式均成立。该证明表明，形状为 $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的每个拉丁杨表的列内容都遵循一种刚性模式，并由此推导出，当在其上方添加长度为 $k+1$ 的新顶行时，每个此类杨表都恰好允许四种有效延拓。因此，对于该形状的所有杨表，顶行 0-1 可用性矩阵的积和式恒等于 4，从而将从形状 $k$ 到形状 $k+1$ 的计数步骤化简为一致乘以 4。结合对基本情况 $k = 5$ 的精确求值（其中形状为 $(5, 4, 3, 3)$ 的拉丁杨表恰好有 144 个，与 $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$ 相符），通项公式便可通过归纳法得出。特别地，该族中的每个形状都是拉丁的，论文指出此前对于 $k \ge 6$ 没有任何结果已知这一点。所有定义、引理以及统领全局的归纳定理均已在 Lean 4 中得到验证。
zh.introduction:
拉丁杨表是对杨图的一种填数，其填入的项沿其行和列均满足拉丁性质。具体而言，对于分拆 $\mu$，形状为 $\mu$ 且型为 $\mu'$ 的拉丁杨表是用正整数对方格集合 $\mu$ 进行填数，使得每行 $i$ 中的项均选自 $\{1, \dots, \mu_i\}$ 且不重复，并且没有正整数在任何列中出现超过一次。由于第 $i$ 行恰好包含 $\mu_i$ 个方格，互异性条件意味着每一行 $i$ 都填有集合 $\{1, 2, \dots, \mu_i\}$ 的一个置换。当杨图是大小为 $n \times n$ 的正方形时，这些结构对应于 $n$ 阶标准拉丁方。对于非矩形图，行长界限与列互异性约束之间的相互作用引入了错综复杂的组合依赖关系。

arXiv:2610.29291 研究了拉丁杨表及其对无限形状族的精确计数。该工作考虑的分拆族包括阶梯形图以及带有修改尾部的类阶梯形。一个具体的形状族由具有双 3 阶梯尾部的形状组成：对于整数 $k \ge 5$，分拆 $\lambda$ 由如下行长序列定义：
$$\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3).$$
该图具有 $k-1$ 个非空行：第一行长度为 $k$，随后的每一行长度依次减少 1 直至达到长度 3，而最后两行的长度均为 3。

在 arXiv:2610.29291 中，猜想 6.3 提出了一个问题，即对于每个整数 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 且型为 $\lambda'$ 的拉丁杨表数目（记为 $LT(\lambda)$）是否由如下精确指数公式给出：
$$LT(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$$
对于最小参数值 $k = 5$，分拆为 $(5, 4, 3, 3)$，猜想的公式预测有 $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$ 个拉丁杨表。论文报告了对于 $k = 6$ 有 576 个杨表，与公式相符；观察到 $(6,5,4,3,3)$ 的每种填数在顶行的前三个方格中都有 $4$、$5$、$6$，在后三个方格中都有 $1$、$2$、$3$；并指出此前没有任何结果已知该族中 $k \ge 6$ 的任何形状是拉丁的。

直接确立此类计数的困难在于杨图延拓的递归本质。在形状为 $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的杨表上方添加长度为 $k+1$ 的新顶行，需要放置 $\{1, 2, \dots, k+1\}$ 的一个置换，使得没有任何项与同列中已有的项发生冲突。一般而言，补全这样一行的方法数取决于基础杨表 $T$ 各列中出现的具体项。对于给定的杨表 $T$，补全数可以表示为一个 $(k+1) \times (k+1)$ 0-1 矩阵的积和式，该矩阵被称为顶行可用性矩阵。因为矩阵积和式在相同形状的不同杨表之间可能会有所不同，所以在大型杨表集合上对积和式求和通常难以化简为闭形式，除非存在很强的结构一致性。

在本篇博文中，我们报告通过定理 `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` 在 Lean 4 中对猜想 6.3 的完整形式化解决。该证明首先确立了该族中所有杨表所共享的刚性列模式，并由此推导出一个结构规律性：对于每个整数 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的每个拉丁杨表都恰好允许四种有效延拓到形状为 $(k+1, k, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的拉丁杨表。也就是说，可用性矩阵的积和式不仅仅是平均为 4；它是逐点不变的，对该族中的每一个杨表都等于 4。这种逐点延拓性质将对所有杨表的求和转化为了标量乘以 4，从而将归纳步骤化简为初等递推。随着基本情况 $k = 5$ 得到形式化确立，闭形式公式 $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$ 对所有 $k \ge 5$ 均成立。
zh.preliminaries:
为了在 Lean 4 中形式化该计数，我们定义了杨图、双 3 尾部分拆族、拉丁杨表集合以及顶行可用性矩阵。我们遵循库中提供的数学结构与 Lean 结构。

杨图 $\mu$ 表示为排列在行和列中的方格集合 $(i, j) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$，其中 $i$ 表示行索引，$j$ 表示列索引。在 Lean 形式化中，行索引和列索引均从 0 开始索引，因此图的左上方格为 $(0, 0)$。第 $i$ 行的长度记为 $\mu.\text{rowLen}(i)$。

定义 1（`latin_double_three_tail_shape`）。对于整数 $k \ge 5$，带有双 3 阶梯尾部的杨图（记为 $\lambda(k)$）是这样一个分拆，其对 $0 \le i < k-1$ 的第 $i$ 行长度由下式给出：
$$\lambda(k).\text{rowLen}(i) = \max(3, k - i),$$
且对所有 $i \ge k-1$ 其行均为空。用序列记号表示，$\lambda(k)$ 的行长为
$$(k, k-1, k-2, \dots, 4, 3, 3),$$
恰好包含 $k-1$ 个非空行。例如，当 $k = 5$ 时，图 $\lambda(5)$ 的行长为 $(5, 4, 3, 3)$。对于 $k = 6$，行长为 $(6, 5, 4, 3, 3)$。

关于索引和空行的注记。Lean 定义 `latin_double_three_tail_shape` 严格在 $i < k - 1$ 时使用从 0 开始索引的公式 $\max(3, k - i)$ 指定行长。对于所有 $i \ge k - 1$，行长隐式为 0。因此，恰好有 $k - 1$ 行非空。最后两个非空行（位于索引 $i = k - 3$ 和 $i = k - 2$ 处）的长度均为 $\max(3, 3) = 3$ 和 $\max(3, 2) = 3$，构成了双 3 尾部。

定义 2（`latin_tableaux`）。设 $\mu$ 为杨图。形状为 $\mu$ 且型为 $\mu'$ 的拉丁杨表是满足以下条件的填数 $T : \mu.\text{cells} \to \mathbb{N}$：

- 行长界限：对于每个方格 $c = (i, j) \in \mu.\text{cells}$，项 $T(c)$ 属于离散区间 $\{1, 2, \dots, \mu.\text{rowLen}(i)\}$。
- 行互异性：对于 $\mu.\text{cells}$ 中满足 $i_1 = i_2$ 的任意两个方格 $c_1 = (i_1, j_1)$ 和 $c_2 = (i_2, j_2)$，若 $T(c_1) = T(c_2)$，则 $j_1 = j_2$。
- 列互异性：对于 $\mu.\text{cells}$ 中满足 $j_1 = j_2$ 的任意两个方格 $c_1 = (i_1, j_1)$ 和 $c_2 = (i_2, j_2)$，若 $T(c_1) = T(c_2)$，则 $i_1 = i_2$。

$\mu$ 上的所有此类拉丁杨表的集合记为 `latin_tableaux` $\mu$。

关于行置换的注记。因为第 $i$ 行恰好包含 $\mu.\text{rowLen}(i)$ 个方格，且每个方格在 $\{1, \dots, \mu.\text{rowLen}(i)\}$ 中取值，所以行单射性条件保证了第 $i$ 行中的项序列是 $\{1, \dots, \mu.\text{rowLen}(i)\}$ 的一个置换。相比之下，整幅图中的列长各不相同，列条件要求在任何一列中都不能有重复的符号。

定义 3（`latin_tableaux_count`）。对于杨图 $\mu$，形状为 $\mu$ 且型为 $\mu'$ 的拉丁杨表数目（记为 $LT(\mu)$）是有穷集（finset）`latin_tableaux` $\mu$ 的基数：
$$LT(\mu) = \#(\text{latin\_tableaux}(\mu)).$$

定义 4（`latin_top_row_availability`）。设 $d$ 为杨图，设 $T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(d)$，并设 $w \in \mathbb{N}$ 表示拟添加到 $T$ 上方的新顶行的宽度。$T$ 对于宽度 $w$ 的顶行可用性矩阵是 $\mathbb{N}$ 上的 $w \times w$ 矩阵，记为 $A(d, T, w)$，对于索引 $i, j \in \{0, 1, \dots, w-1\}$ 定义为
$$A(d, T, w)_{i, j} = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{if for all } c \in d.\text{cells} \text{ with } c.\text{col} = j, \text{ we have } T(c) \neq i + 1, \\
0 & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}$$

关于候选符号与列的注记。在 `latin_top_row_availability` 中，矩阵的行索引候选符号 $s = i + 1 \in \{1, \dots, w\}$，而矩阵的列索引杨表的列 $j \in \{0, \dots, w-1\}$。当且仅当将符号 $i + 1$ 放入列 $j$ 不会与 $T$ 的列 $j$ 中的任何方格产生列冲突时，矩阵元为 1。完整放置长度为 $w$ 的有效顶行对应于符号与可用性为 1 的列之间的双射，此类有效顶行的总数由 $A(d, T, w)$ 的积和式给出。
zh.result:
主定理确立了 arXiv:2610.29291 中猜想 6.3 的有效性，给出了带有双 3 阶梯尾部的拉丁杨表数目的精确指数公式。

定理（`latin_double_three_tail_count_formula`）。对于每个整数 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $\lambda(k) = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 且型为 $\lambda(k)'$ 的拉丁杨表数目由下式给出：
$$LT(\lambda(k)) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}.$$

在 Lean 4 中，该定理命名为 `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula`。其陈述接收一个自然数 $k$，假定假设 $5 \le k$，应用 `latin_double_three_tail_shape` 构造杨图，并断言 `latin_tableaux_count` 等于 $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$。

除了主公式外，形式化推导还提供了三项基础性结果：

- 基本情况计数（`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`）：对于 $k = 5$，杨图的形状为 $(5, 4, 3, 3)$，拉丁杨表的数目恰好为 144，验证了 $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$。
- 归纳步骤公式（`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`）：对于每个 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $\lambda(k+1)$ 的拉丁杨表数目等于对形状为 $\lambda(k)$ 的所有拉丁杨表的顶行可用性矩阵的积和式之和。
- 逐点四延拓性质（`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`）：对于每个 $k \ge 5$ 以及形状为 $\lambda(k)$ 的每个拉丁杨表 $T$，宽度为 $k+1$ 的顶行可用性矩阵的积和式恒等于 4。
zh.proof:
我们遵循在 Lean 4 中验证的形式化论证给出 `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` 的证明。

证明的思路是对 $k \ge 5$ 进行归纳。$k = 5$ 时的基本情况通过对形状为 $(5, 4, 3, 3)$ 的杨表有限集合进行穷举计算得到验证。对于归纳步骤，在形状为 $\lambda(k) = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的杨表顶端添加长度为 $k+1$ 的行，会得到形状为 $\lambda(k+1) = (k+1, k, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的杨表。在不违背列互异性的前提下填入该顶行的方法数等于可用性矩阵的积和式。形状为 $\lambda(k)$ 的每个杨表都具有相同的列内容刚性模式，并由此得出其可用性积和式恒等于 4，因此积和式之和可以分解为 4 乘以形状为 $\lambda(k)$ 的 `latin_tableaux` 的基数。应用归纳假设便将该步骤化简为初等指数算术。

引理 1（`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`）。形状为 $(5, 4, 3, 3)$ 的拉丁杨表数目满足
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } 5) = 144.$$

*引理 1 的证明。* 杨图 $\lambda(5)$ 的行长为 $(5, 4, 3, 3)$，总共包含 $5 + 4 + 3 + 3 = 15$ 个方格。杨表是向每个方格 $(i, j)$ 赋予 $\{1, \dots, \lambda(5).\text{rowLen}(i)\}$ 中的值，使得各项在每行中互异且在每列中互异。因为方格集合是有穷的且可能填数的集合是有穷的，所以 Lean 可以计算经过滤的拉丁杨表有穷集的基数。该计算搜索了在这 15 个方格上满足列单射性的所有有效行置换。该验证确认恰好有 144 种填数满足所有约束。注意到 $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 4^2 = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$，基本情况成立。

引理 2（`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`）。对于任意整数 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $\lambda(k+1)$ 的拉丁杨表数目满足
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape}(k+1)) = \sum_{T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)} \text{Matrix.permanent}(\text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)).$$

*引理 2 的证明。* 这是在论文自身的积和式递推（其引理 5.4）中插入一个新首行的情况。形状为 $\lambda(k+1) = (k+1, k, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的任何杨表 $T'$ 都可以唯一分解为其顶行（长度为 $k+1$ 的第 0 行）和其余 $k-1$ 行。将下方的各行向上平移一个索引，即得到形状为 $\lambda(k) = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的杨表 $T$。第 0 行的项必须构成 $\{1, 2, \dots, k+1\}$ 的一个置换，使得对于每一列 $j \in \{0, \dots, k\}$，放置在 $(0, j)$ 处的数值不会出现在 $T$ 的列 $j$ 中。根据可用性矩阵 $M = \text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)$ 的定义，矩阵元 $M_{i, j}$ 等于 1 当且仅当符号 $i+1$ 在列 $j$ 中可用。因此，一个有效顶行对应于一个双射 $\sigma : \{0, \dots, k\} \to \{0, \dots, k\}$，使得对所有 $j$ 均有 $M_{\sigma(j), j} = 1$。此类双射的数目就是 $M$ 的积和式。对形状为 $\lambda(k)$ 的所有杨表 $T$ 的所有有效补全进行求和，便得到了该等式。

引理 3（`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`）。对于任意整数 $k \ge 5$ 以及每个拉丁杨表 $T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)$，宽度为 $k+1$ 的顶行可用性矩阵的积和式为 4：
$$\text{Matrix.permanent}(\text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)) = 4.$$

*引理 3 的证明。* Lean 证明考察了各列的符号集合。在 $\lambda(k)$ 中（列从 0 开始索引），列 $0, 1, 2$ 各有 $k-1$ 个方格，而对 $3 \le j \le k-1$，列 $j$ 有 $k-j$ 个方格；特别地，列 $k-2$ 有两个方格，列 $k-1$ 有一个方格。若存在 $s \in \{1,2,3\}$ 和 $c \in \{0,1,2\}$ 满足以下条件，则称形状为 $\lambda(k)$ 的杨表 $T$ 具有*规范轮廓*（canonical profile）：

- 列 $c$ 包含符号 $\{1, \dots, k-2\} \cup \{k\}$，而列 $0, 1, 2$ 中的另外两列包含 $\{1, \dots, k-1\}$；
- 对 $3 \le j \le k-3$，列 $j$ 包含 $\{1, \dots, k-j\}$；
- 列 $k-2$ 包含 $\{1,2,3\} \setminus \{s\}$，列 $k-1$ 包含 $\{s\}$。

*步骤 (a)：形状为 $\lambda(k)$（$k \ge 5$）的每个杨表都具有规范轮廓。* 这是对 $k$ 的归纳法。对于 $k = 5$，它在形状为 $(5,4,3,3)$ 的所有杨表上得到检验。对于归纳步骤，形状为 $\lambda(k+1)$ 的杨表是一个形状为 $\lambda(k)$ 的杨表 $T$ 并在其上方放置了长度为 $k+1$ 的顶行；根据归纳假设，$T$ 具有规范轮廓，并且下文步骤 (b) 的分析展示了顶行可以在每一列中放置哪些符号。将它们添加到 $T$ 的列集合中即可得到形状为 $\lambda(k+1)$ 的规范轮廓：列 $0, 1, 2$ 中包含 $\{1,\dots,k-1\}$ 的两列接收 $k$ 和 $k+1$，其中一列变为 $\{1,\dots,k\}$，另一列变为 $\{1,\dots,k-1\} \cup \{k+1\}$；列 $c$ 接收 $k-1$ 并变为 $\{1,\dots,k\}$；满足 $3 \le j \le k-3$ 的列 $j$ 接收 $k-j+1$；列 $k-2$ 接收 $s$ 并变为 $\{1,2,3\}$；列 $k-1$ 和列 $k$ 接收 $\{1,2,3\} \setminus \{s\}$ 中的两个符号，使得列 $k-1$ 包含 $\{1,2,3\}$ 中的两个符号，而列 $k$ 包含第三个符号。

*步骤 (b)：具有规范轮廓的杨表恰好有四个长度为 $k+1$ 的有效顶行。* 顶行是从列 $0, \dots, k$ 到符号 $1, \dots, k+1$ 的双射，且没有任何符号被放置在已经包含它的列中。列 $0, 1, 2$ 中包含 $\{1,\dots,k-1\}$ 的两列只能取 $k$ 和 $k+1$，因此它们恰好取这两个符号，有两种可能顺序。列 $c$ 随后只能取 $k-1$。向右推进，对于 $j = 3, \dots, k-3$，列 $j$ 只能取至少为 $k-j+1$ 的符号，而所有更大的符号均已被使用，因此它取 $k-j+1$；这用尽了 $4, \dots, k-2$。符号 $1, 2, 3$ 留给列 $k-2$、$k-1$、$k$。列 $k-2$ 包含 $\{1,2,3\} \setminus \{s\}$，因此它取 $s$，而列 $k-1$ 和列 $k$ 以任意顺序取其余两个符号（列 $k-1$ 仅包含 $s$，而列 $k$ 为空）。这给出了 $2 \cdot 2 = 4$ 个顶行，因此可用性矩阵的积和式为 4。

*主定理的证明。* 我们结合引理 1、2 和 3，通过对 $k \ge 5$ 的归纳法证明 `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula`。

在基本情况 $k = 5$ 下，引理 1（`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`）确立了
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } 5) = 144.$$
由于 $9 \cdot 4^{5-3} = 9 \cdot 4^2 = 9 \cdot 16 = 144$，基本情况通过直接数值计算成立。

对于归纳步骤，作为归纳假设，假定对某个 $k \ge 5$，
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) = 9 \cdot 4^{k-3}.$$
我们希望计算 $k+1$ 时的计数。应用引理 2（`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`），我们将形状为 $\lambda(k+1)$ 的杨表计数写为
$$\sum_{T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)} \text{Matrix.permanent}(\text{latin\_top\_row\_availability}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \, T \, (k+1)).$$
根据引理 3（`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`），该和式中的每一项均恒为 4。在整个求和中将每个积和式替换为 4 可得
$$\sum_{T \in \text{latin\_tableaux}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k)} 4.$$
在拉丁杨表的有限集上对常数 4 求和产生乘积
$$\text{latin\_tableaux\_count}(\text{latin\_double\_three\_tail\_shape } k) \cdot 4.$$
将归纳假设代入该表达式得出
$$(9 \cdot 4^{k-3}) \cdot 4.$$
由于 $k \ge 5$，指数算术满足 $(k+1) - 3 = (k - 3) + 1$，并且根据指数运算法则 $4^{(k-3)+1} = 4^{k-3} \cdot 4$。重写该乘积得到
$$9 \cdot 4^{(k+1)-3},$$
这完成了归纳步骤，并证明了定理对所有 $k \ge 5$ 均成立。
zh.discussion:
定理 `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` 彻底解决了 arXiv:2610.29291 中的猜想 6.3。所提出的问题询问对于每个整数 $k \ge 5$，形状为 $\lambda = (k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 且型为 $\lambda'$ 的拉丁杨表数目是否等于 $9 \cdot 4^{k-3}$。该定理在完全一般性上确立了这一等式，对整个无限族肯定地回答了该问题。

由于 $9 \cdot 4^{k-3} > 0$，每个满足 $k \ge 5$ 的形状 $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 都是拉丁的。论文指出，此前没有任何结果已知该族中 $k \ge 6$ 的任何形状是拉丁的，并且即便是对于 $(6,5,4,3,3)$ 也需要一种新技术；上述列轮廓论证就是这样一种适用于整个族的技术。

该证明策略依赖于引理 3（`latin_double_three_tail_four_extensions`）中表述的逐点四延拓性质，并结合了引理 2（`latin_double_three_tail_count_step`）中的归纳步骤以及引理 1（`latin_double_three_tail_count_base`）中的基本求值。在拉丁杨表的一般计数问题中，通过新行延拓杨表的方法数可能会根据各个杨表的列项而发生显著变化。然而在本文中，形状为 $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的每个杨表都具有一个积和式恒等于 4 的可用性矩阵。这种一致行为将步骤公式中的积和式之和直接化简为标量乘以 4。

关于该结果未涵盖的方面，此计数严格适用于带有双 3 阶梯尾部的杨图族：

- 该定理针对 $k \ge 5$（即猜想 6.3 的范围）进行陈述；更小的 $k$ 未作讨论。
- 该结果不涵盖形状不同于 $(k, k-1, \dots, 4, 3, 3)$ 的杨表，例如具有不同尾部长度的阶梯形或具有其他分拆结构的杨图。

最后，所提供的源材料未提及除猜想 6.3 之外的其他公开问题或猜想。由于 `latin_double_three_tail_count_formula` 证明了对所有 $k \ge 5$ 的精确公式，arXiv:2610.29291 中关于该无限族提出的问题已彻底解决。
